utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, would you stand up, please, and make the solemn declaration in the document that the court usher is giving to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, madam. Thank you. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning Witness 115. I'd ask you to sit back and relax and there's some water there. Feel free to have a drink any time you need during your testimony here today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, madam. Because of the voice distortion, you've got to turn your microphone off. Having trained you to turn it on, remember to turn it off because otherwise her voice will go through the ordinary system. Sorry, madam. That is just for your protection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where do I turn it off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no. Yours is all right. It was counsel's microphone that I was asking him to turn it off so that your voice would not go through the normal system. Your microphone there is the one with the voice distortion in it, so you need not worry. Now, you were asked -- you hadn't been asked a question. Off you go, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the witness be shown her pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would ask the witness: Is that your name and your birth date on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P81, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, I would ask you to briefly describe your educational back ground for the Court, without specifying what schools you may have attended.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I went to the higher school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that post-secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you to briefly describe for the Court your professional background, again without specifying any specific companies you may have worked for.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I worked for 14 years in [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you please tell the Court, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I am a Serb by ethnicity, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you marry a person of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the early summer of 1992 and ask you: At that time did you move to live temporarily in the area of Pionirska Street in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that time was there a curfew in the town or were the Serbs in the town informed of a curfew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. That was compulsory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what time the curfew was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Between 8.00 and 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the house that you stayed in temporarily in Pionirska Street, did you also own a house in another part of town, without telling us that part of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and it was a newly built house. My own property, my own house, in which I never actually lived; I never succeeded in living in the house I'd built.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in the early summer of 1992, when you were temporarily living in Pionirska Street, did you see people or two persons you knew to be Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you first saw them after moving to Pionirska Street, did you see them in a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: In a red Passat-type car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know who the owner of that car was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The former owner was a lady. Her name was Behija and she was from the Dusce part of Visegrad. She had a shop selling vegetables, a grocery store selling fruit and vegetables. I don't remember her surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a third person with Mr. Lukic and Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. There was a third person behind whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was driving this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at this time in the area of Pionirska Street, would it be fair to say that many of the Muslim residents had fled the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Mostly they all fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And in the course of their fleeing, was it common for lights to be left on in the houses that these Muslim people had abandoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Some people probably came to take things clandestinely and left the lights on. Probably that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to describe for the Court: What did you observe Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic do this first time you saw them on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, it would be of more assistance if before we did that, we a ascertained from her, if necessary in private session, how she knew them. Isn't that rather important?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was going to do that at the end, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we've been through this before. Logically it would be preferable to have that before we hear the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And we can do that in public session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, before you answer that question, I would ask you to describe for the Court how is it that you knew Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I have known Mr. Vasiljevic. He worked in catering in Visegrad in Panos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you yourself frequent that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was more for men. They played a game, tombola, and I would pass by the door every day along the pavement, that's in Visegrad, but I very rarely entered. My husband would frequent the place more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to seeing Mr. Vasiljevic on Pionirska Street, can you describe for us approximately how many times you would have seen Mr. Vasiljevic before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Before that day, I can't remember how many times I saw him, because it was wartime in Visegrad, but under normal conditions, while everything was normal, the atmosphere was normal and people went around town, I would see him often.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to look around the courtroom here today and tell us whether you recognise the person you're describing as Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise him. He's sitting wearing a brown suit, but he's put on a lot of weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you tell us where he's sitting in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He's sitting to the left, that is, to the right of the policeman. Is it the right or the left? Which way do you want it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There's only one person wearing a brown coat in the whole courtroom and that is the accused, so I think you've made that point. Very well

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: With a tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 115. Your Honour, may the record reflect the witness has identified the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to return to this first sighting of Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What about the Lukic? It's the same problem we're going to get throughout these cases unless you tell us how they know the -- the witnesses know these people, we're left up in the air the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, would you please describe for us how you knew Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I didn't know Milan Lukic from before, when times from normal in Visegrad. At that time he was a very young man, nice, tall, dark. He came from the surroundings of Belgrade, Obrenovac, but otherwise he is a native of Bosnia, and I think he comes from a village called Rujiste, actually. I had occasion to meet Milan personally at work, in the offices I worked in, both before the war and after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you to go to the point in time that you were describing seeing these two men in the red Passat. Would you please describe what you observed them do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: In the red Passat, they came prior to curfew. It was already dusk. They came to Pionirska Street, where I was residing temporarily, because my husband had already left Visegrad. I was collecting papers and documents for my children. And when I was going down the steps in the house that I lived in, I thought that it was a car coming from my own company to look for me personally. But when I approached the car, I realised which car it was and I assumed who was inside. That was my first meeting with Milan. He got out of the car. He was a little arrogant in his behaviour, asked me where my husband was. I told him where he had gone, that he was on official business, on a business trip. I said that -- I told him the town my husband had gone to and said that my parents lived there. He shouted at me and asked me why the lights were on, asked whether there were any Muslims roundabout. I said I didn't know whether there was anybody. I didn't think so. Then I recognised Mitar next to him. There was a third person lying down in the seat behind, probably I didn't know that person. When I mentioned the town to which my husband had gone, that third person reacted all of a sudden because he was probably from that particular town himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, I'd ask you to describe what was Mitar Vasiljevic doing at the time you were having with conversation with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic was sitting. He wasn't doing anything. He didn't ask me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did all of the men remain inside the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: They remained in the car. They went round in circles in the lower street, the parallel street to Pionirska Street, above which I lived. They received information that in a large house there, there were two elderly persons: An elderly man from Koritnik and his old grandmother from Koritnik. Their surname was Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, before leaving did they ask you to show them any documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't ask me anything, and that was lucky. They didn't ask me at that moment what my husband's name was, so they knew nothing at that particular moment. They just asked me where my husband was. They didn't know my name or his, so I didn't actually say my name and they didn't ask for documents either. They didn't ask for anything, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Not long. Very short. Five or six minutes, perhaps, ten at the most. Not long. I was very frightened, but they left very quickly. They didn't go into any of the houses. They looked through the lower street and they had probably received information, and then they went into the Kurspahic house with a battery, with a lamp. It was dark, and they found the old people on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, the area that you were staying in, would it be fair to say that that was a predominantly Muslim area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was a mixed population.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how about this other street that you say you saw them drive to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: In the other street there were both Muslim houses and Serb houses on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described them going to the house of an elderly couple by the name of Kurspahic from Koritnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the approximate age of this couple?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: About 70. And during the day when I came back from work, I saw the old woman. She was digging in the garden. And I told her that it wasn't a good idea for her to be outside at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court where in relation is the house belonging to the Kurspahics from the house that you were staying in at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The courtyards border on each other, but the house I was in is a higher house, but parallel, below the house I was living in, and there wasn't a partition between the courtyards of those two houses either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether the lights were on or off in this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The lights were off. They were hiding, the old people were hiding on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you see a flashlight inside that darkened house at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. They searched the house with flashlights. They went right up to the third floor, second floor, and first floor, searching.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see the red Passat from where you were at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The house is a big one, and the Passat was parked right below the Kurspahic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to see Milan Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, or this other person during the time you are now describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was able to all the time that they went in and searched the house from the third floor to the first floor, because the Kurspahic house is parallel to the terrace and windows where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were able to determine that they found the Kurspahic couple inside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The lights went on on the first floor. They made some noise and asked where their sons were and called out the sons' names. The old woman entreated them not to kill them, and it all lasted for a very brief moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "the old woman entreated them not to kill them," were you able to determine who she was referring to when she was using the word "them"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic, and a third person whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to determine whether she was referring to her sons or to her and her husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: She was screaming. She said that her -- she didn't know anything about her sons, that they're clean, that they had done nothing, and they said, "Please don't kill us." However, there was a burst of gunfire. It was all very terrible. And I heard the screams of the old woman. They killed the old man first and then there was a burst of gunfire and then they killed the old woman too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next day, did you happen to go in front -- by the front of that building of the Kurspahic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The next morning I had to go to work. The doors were open -- the door was open and their legs were sticking out. It was a terrible sight and I was very much afraid all through the night and all through the day and all through the ensuing days that I spent in the town. The body was there for more than five or six days, until somebody finally took it away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time during your stay on Pionirska Street or in the area of Pionirska Street that you became aware of a fire in which people from Koritnik lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: As to the fire, I do know about the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is your best recollection as to when this fire occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The fire broke out while there was a curfew on round the clock, non-stop. It was towards dusk, at the end of June. I was going up to the [redacted] Mitar Vasiljevic, with his group of men, was taking a mass of people. There were some elderly people there, older people, younger people, women, children. They were taking them upwards Pionirska Street, which is the street that I passed by every day until I left that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, were you staying in the same house that you just told us you were staying in Pionirska Street when you observed the death of the Kurspahic couple?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This night, did you stay in a different house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was in a different house. It also belonged to the [redacted], which is quite a bit lower than the other one. But they're related. And I had to go with my child to look for safety, to see where to hide, where to take refuge, because it wasn't safe anywhere. And my daughter was with me. That was the child that was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court where this second house is that you stayed in in relation to the school that's on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you please tell us? Will you please describe where this second house is in relation to the school on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Oh, I see. In relation to the schoolhouse, the school and house are on the right-hand side. The school is a higher building than the house that I was in. So when I come from the centre of town, up the hill of Pionirska Street, both the school and the house are to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, were you coming up Pionirska Street from town at the time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was coming from town. The column was exactly in front of me, so that I had no chance of turning left or right or going back. I was afraid. I didn't know what was going on myself. A lady - I don't want to mention her name - was coming towards me, and she left the group. She was well known to me. She was a neighbour of mine, a friend of mine. We used to have coffee. He said, "You go with the people," but she didn't want to, and she is alive and well and living in a town in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When she -- when you saw her, which direction was she travelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: She was going down Pionirska Street, coming towards the group, and she went towards town. I couldn't help her. We just -- our eyes met, that's all. We glanced at each other and I didn't dare do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you hear Mitar Vasiljevic say anything to this woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. He told her to go with the people and to join the group. She said, "I don't want to and I'm not going to." But Mitar didn't do anything bad. He didn't react at all. He just went on with his assignment. He had this mass of people in front of him and his associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you hear Mitar Vasiljevic say anything to the group or to the remainder of the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He just told them to go forward, to move forward. I didn't dare pay any more attention, I was so afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see Milan Lukic here at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Of course. I did see him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see Mitar Vasiljevic with a megaphone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any of the men in the group with a megaphone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I just heard somebody speaking over the megaphone, but I don't remember that it was Mitar Vasiljevic but that was very short, brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go after you saw this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I went to [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that the house that you stayed in that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 17.4. I will ask her to make a mark on it, so I ask that we deem this 17.4, 115, to indicate she is the witness marking on this copy of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by deem it. We'll admit it as that document when she has done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's what I mean, Your Honour. I would ask that it be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, I would ask that you take the pen next to you and just write the number 115 on the bottom of that photograph to indicate that it's you that's making marks on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Where do you want me to write the number? On the photograph itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, on the photograph itself, somewhere near the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The bottom of the house or the whole photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No. Just on the bottom of the photograph. Would you just put your witness identification number, number 115, so we know you drew on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I understand now. I understand. I've put 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The first thing I'm going to ask you to do is to draw an "X" to indicate where it was that you saw this group of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: First saw, you mean, when you first saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. Where you first saw this group of people as they were coming up Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Shall I put a cross there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask the witness to identify the house that she was in, since this will reveal her identity, I would ask that we go into private session for just a few moments and allow her to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure that I can see where the cross is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Private session, please. I can't see where the cross is. Is it at that intersection there, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, do you object to the tender of this exhibit as 17/115 -- I'm sorry 17/4, and then-115?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P17/4.115, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, after you went to this house that you've just indicated to us, did you remain there for the course of the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time later on that day or later that night that you heard some activity outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, of course I did. It was nearby. I'm sorry, I'm unable to show the house where this was happening. My mind was going, and forgive me for this. I was full of fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how much time had transpired between the time you entered this house and the time you heard something outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Perhaps over half an hour. These activities didn't start immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what you heard from the house that you were in at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Powerful explosions were heard, shooting, cries and screams of the people, then smoke could be smelled in the air, burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you went to the balcony of the house you were staying in and try to look at what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was extremely afraid. I was running around the house. This is a two-storey building and I ran from one window to another. The windows faced three different sides, as did the balconies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see the area where the sounds were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The house that I was in is on the right-hand side, and the sounds were coming from the left-hand side, very nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the creek that runs in the area of Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. It's a creek between the settlement of Glavica and Pionirska Street. It has very little water in it. It is almost dry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where the sounds were coming from in relation to that creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The sounds were coming from between the creek and Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how long did these sounds go on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The sounds of burning and everything else lasted an hour and a half, maybe up to two hours. It went on for a long time. That is to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are we going to be able to get any identification of the approximate time? At the moment it's just later that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll ask her that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it dark at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, of course it was dark. Yes, it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is your best estimate or best recollection of the time that you first began to hear the sounds coming from this direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I think it was early evening. I'm afraid it was a long time ago for me to be more precise, but I think it was after 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could you smell anything at the time you heard these sounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I could smell smoke, and there were powerful explosions and the smell of smoke could be felt. People were burning in horror, the burning of human flesh could be smelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time that you heard these sounds, were you able or did you see Mitar Vasiljevic in the area at the time you heard these sounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: In that area, I mean, at the time the cries were heard, I was unable to see him, because one couldn't look really. I would have -- people, when the curfew was on, would pull down the blinds and switch off the lights. That is what we all had to do in the town of Visegrad. But still, I peeped out, prompted by the horror of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you did not see him at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I could not see him then. Even if I wanted to, there was a large group of people with Mitar who were doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see Milan Lukic at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I couldn't. I couldn't recognise anyone from among the people who were doing this. I could not recognise anyone. It was already dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I think you've told us this already, but just to be clear: Your best recollection as to the day that this happened is that it happened in late June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, quite. That is correct, according to my recollection. It was a long time ago, ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The morning after the fire, did you speak to a neighbour, without telling us his name, did you speak to a neighbour regarding what happened the night before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I didn't sleep that night from fear. In the morning I set off to work quite early. I had to leave the house. And I saw the neighbour, or my former landowner, and he was carrying water in a plastic can to assist somebody in the house. Somebody must have survived in that house. Somebody did survive. It wasn't important whether it was a man or a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he describe for you where that survivor -- where he found that survivor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you please describe for us where he told you he found that survivor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Before we had met, he had probably gone to that house earlier and around the house and towards the creek, and he found a person with big burns, and he said that the two- or three-day-old baby had been burnt to death, and I assume that he was carrying water for that lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of this neighbour? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us what his reaction was to his discovery that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The man was out of his mind. He was worse than me, only he had the courage to move around; I didn't. It wasn't a young man. His sons were my generation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, would it be fair to say that you remained in Visegrad -- remained living in Visegrad up until early 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I had to. I couldn't flee. They wouldn't give me a passport. I was almost in captivity. I was under work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time later in the summer of 1992 that you saw the accused Mitar Vasiljevic with a cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I saw him with a cast, but in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us your best recollection of the first time or the date of the first time you saw him with a cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I think it was in the autumn. It was colder. Maybe September or October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that time did you also see him walking with crutches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: A couple of times I did see him with crutches. On one occasion I saw him on a horse.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was he riding the horse with the cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It seemed to me that he had a cast on his leg when he was on horseback, though this wasn't important for me. I didn't look closely. I didn't look at those people at all. I always hid from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know who owned the horse that he was riding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw you back to the summer of 1992, shortly after the fire on Pionirska Street. I'd ask you, did you observe an incident involving a person by the name of Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court your best recollection of when you observed this incident of Kahriman in relation to the fire on Pionirska Street, how much time between the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Between the two incidents, this was the end of June. I had already moved into housing, apartment building, so it was at the end of June or the beginning of July. It was hot that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this apartment that you moved into, would it be fair to characterise this as being in the centre of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Visegrad is a very small town, so everything is in the centre. The apartment I lived in belongs to the part of town known as [redacted],

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. The question you asked earlier was a very leading one. I would like to see if you can ask her a question which enables her to say when this was in relation to the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not much help if you lead them into these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will you please describe for us as best you're able the number of days or the number of weeks between the fire in Pionirska Street and the incident involving a man by the name of Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's still a leading question. What we want to know is what happened first. This is going to be the issue here, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 115, which occurred first, the fire on Pionirska Street or the incident involving Mr. Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. First the fire occurred, and after that fire, after that horror, I had nothing to do with Pionirska Street. I fled from there and I found accommodation in an apartment that belonged to my company, with the help of my - how shall I put it? - my bosses, I was given this apartment to use, and I moved in with my daughter and I stayed there until I fled, and that was at the beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If I may say so, that should teach you that if you ask her a non-leading question, you'll get a better answer. I'm sorry, but this sort of thing is vital. Try to avoid leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you estimate the number of days or weeks or time period between the fire and this incident with Mr. Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Am I supposed to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate the time period between these two events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It wasn't long. It was a short time period. Don't forget that things were happening in Visegrad at great speed. They followed one another. And the suffering was awful. In June, July, and August, the suffering of the Muslim people. And the events followed one another at great speed. So I would say the beginning of July, when the incident with the old man Kahriman from Dusce occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you please describe for us the people who were involved in that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was in the afternoon, when I was going back from work. I was crossing the new bridge. I had no transportation that day, so I went on foot. And this incident was taking place close to my building. An innocent man was being mistreated in all kinds of ways. Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic, and Slobodan Roncevic and Jovo Lipovac were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe how this man was being mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The man was on my right as I was approaching the building. And there were a lot of citizens, a lot of my colleagues were coming home from work. There were passersby. This was daytime, it wasn't night-time. It was daylight. They were mistreating the man. I saw that he had handcuffs on. He was screaming. They were making cuts on his arms. After that they cut his ears and mistreated him, because he was the father of an alleged well-known extremist known as Cabre or his uncle, I don't know which.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Mitar Vasiljevic have anything covering his face or disguising himself on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't. I was able to see Mitar. He wasn't masked. No one was masked. According to the stories of my colleagues, they may have used masks in the evening when they killed their neighbours so they wouldn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you leave this incident before it was concluded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was there very briefly. I couldn't walk properly. The man was screaming. I was out of my mind. I didn't know whether I was normal any more. I had some pills on me. I took those pills. And one couldn't forget those screams. If it wasn't for my daughter, I would have killed myself, but I had to go on living because of my daughter, who was a minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you learn whether or not the man was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Of course. The body could be seen for a long time. It ended up in the Drina, like the others, eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after this event that you were in a friend's house and you heard the person you've referred to as Slobodan Roncevic talk about this attack on Mr. Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. This was a young man, a student from Novi Sad, Slobodan Roncevic. He came to visit my friend. We were having coffee together. She was unmarried and so was he, I think, and he recounted the story, enjoying every moment of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During this event that you witnessed, were you able to tell whether Mitar Vasiljevic had a cast on his leg at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I didn't notice it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to an event involving a Medo Mulahasic. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was his approximate age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He was over 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This event you're about to describe, did this happen before or after the fire on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: After the fire. I was surprised to see Muslims in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did this event happen before or after the event you've just described with Mr. Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: After. After Kahriman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, can you tell us the time period between what you observed with Mr. Kahriman and what you observed with Mr. Mulahasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: This incident occurred at the end of July 1992. The killing took place on the old bridge next to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was carrying some commercial products for my company. I had my driver. The car was parked in front of the department store. I got out and I saw a skinny man with his back bent, being led by children. Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic across the square. I looked closer and I saw that it was Medo Mulahasic. They gave him a cigarette to smoke. I can't forget that. So the citizens of Visegrad were teaching small boys to wage war. They may have had 12, 13, or 14 to shoot at people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you at the time that you were making this observation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I was on the square, the square in the town of Visegrad, between the hotel and the department store. The old bridge is nearby, the Cuprija, known as the Cuprija.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you on foot or were you in a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No. I had to walk to the car. I was always in the car. I didn't dare walk a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On this occasion when you saw Mr. Vasiljevic, was there anything disguising or covering his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, nothing. He didn't have anything on him. This was before noon. My business between -- [redacted] [redacted] place between 11.00 and 12.00, so it was daytime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Milan Lukic, was there anything covering or disguising his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No. He never disguised himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see what happened on the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: They shot at the back of his head and they threw him over the stone wall into the Drina, at the small back of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And at this time, are you able to tell us whether or not he had a cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I don't remember. I would be more prone to say that he didn't have a cast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to an incident that you witnessed involving a person with the nickname Kupus, or cabbage. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I do remember that incident. This incident also occurred towards the end of July, on a small bridge known as the Rzav bridge, there is a small tributary of the Drina flowing below that bridge. It is called the Rzav, and this small bridge is in the centre of town. We were going home from work through town. There were other colleagues with me. I'd rather not mention their names, because they are important to me. And at the small bridge, next to an iron fence, Kupus was standing. I don't know his first or last name. He used to sell tickets in a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us what people you saw involved in this incident with Kupus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I saw Milan Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and another of the Lukics. I lost a sandal. It was very hot, and Mitar yelled at me to hurry along so as not to end up like this man. They were hitting him. They were stabbing him with a knife. He was screaming. It was terrible. It was in daytime. People were passing by. They scared people. They were intimidating their own people, because only Serbs had remained, and they too lived in terror and in fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time was there anything covering or disguising Mitar Vasiljevic's face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you be more precise about what you saw each of these men do in relation to Mr. Kupus? I'd ask you to begin by describing what Milan Lukic did to this man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Milan Lukic stabbed him with a knife lots of times, lots of times, all over his body, and Mitar was right up against this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you see whether he was holding the man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He didn't have to hold him. The man didn't dare budge. His hands were up against an iron railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how far were you from this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 to 20 steps away, on the other side of the little bridge and the railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did there come a time when Mitar Vasiljevic spoke directly to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He only told me to hurry up. I was so afraid, and something fell off me, my leg, and he said, "Pass by quickly so that you don't end up like this as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During this incident, are you able to tell us whether or not he had a cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything. I was too afraid. I was in a hurry. I hurried, like all my other friends, girls.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 115. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam 115, when you began your testimony here this morning, in answer to a question from Mr. Groome about your ethnicity, if I remember correctly, you said that you were a Serb, and then you added "unfortunately."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Remember to turn your microphone off when she is answering, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you explain to me why you said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Can you not assume that for yourself? Don't you know the answer yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Perhaps I can, madam, but I would like to have your opinion and explanation, not my own surmise and conjecture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: My opinion is that Mr. Vasiljevic and all members of that group were of the Serb ethnicity, just like me, and I'm ashamed of that. I'm ashamed of the place where I was born. I love the town. I love the town of Visegrad and I haven't seen it for ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, however, you stayed on in that town until the beginning --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, you're right, sir. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You stayed on until 1994. Would you please, madam, not interrupt me, because of the interpreters and the microphone. So wait until I finish my question. You stayed on in Visegrad, and as far as I can see, you had no problems. You were free to leave, you are free to go back. So perhaps there is another reason why you don't wish to live in Visegrad any more.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Your Honour, Judge, that is not true. I cannot live in Visegrad any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, you gave a statement to the investigator of the Prosecution at the beginning of this year, or rather, in the course of this year; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: At the beginning -- or perhaps it was last year. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. But you made a statement, one statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you gave your particulars, in the faith column you answered "none," your answer was "none." Could you tell us the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Would you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Let me repeat my question. In the statement, in the column for religion, in that column you state "none." You say you have no religion. Can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: You're asking me about my religion, faith, that column?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well, madam. Let me rephrase the question. Perhaps that will help you. Your religion or faith, if you have it, what is it? What is your faith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: My faith or religion, I am a Serb, because my parents are Serbs. Both my parents are Serbs. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Not all Serbs are of the same religion. Religion is something different. Can you explain that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Religion. I'm not a religious person. I haven't been trained, brought up in the faith, religiously, and I had nothing much to do with my parents, nothing to do with my parents. I went to school. I wasn't tied to religion of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. That answers the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you personally see the release of the water from the dam by a certain Murat, and what happened after that? I think you mentioned it. Can you tell us more about that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The release of the water and the dam, I don't know the date now, and dates are always a problem for me, but it was much earlier on, much earlier than what I was talking about in my testimony. It looked terrible. Visegrad looked terrible when the water was released. Now, if you're asking me about Murat and Avdija, they are people, two men from Dusce. They were extremists before the war as well. They were of an extremist orientation. Now, when I say "extremist," I mean that they would, for example, stop cars randomly, passing over bridges, they would stop buses. They did this before the war too. They fought before the war. And they were dishonest citizens. I didn't know them personally myself, but as a family, they're on the minus side, not plus side. They weren't good citizens as far as Visegrad is concerned, and did a lot of damage by releasing the Drina. There was chaos in town as a result of it. The population dispersed, and that day was a horrible day to remember. We had to flee to the centre of town. All the surrounding villages had to flee into town to find an escape. When the water was released, I personally too had to take to the hills. We all took to the hills, towards Bikavac, to avoid being flooded and drowned in the water. It was terrible. There was general darkness in town, a fog. The water took away with it houses and trees and the whole scene was terrible. So that in those few days, I was divided from my husband, and I went to Prijepolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You speak of the height of the waves in your statement. You say they were 10 or more metres high.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it looked like, perhaps even higher. That's what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did those waves take a bridge with them which was above Visegrad towards Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. The bridge was near the power plant and it was destroyed by the flood, and many of the houses on the banks of the Drina and the trees were uprooted. Everything that was located along the banks of the Drina was destroyed by the flood, by the waters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can we say, then, madam, that at that time, because of that situation, the town of Visegrad was practically empty, that all the Muslim and Serb population had left the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Practically nobody remained in town. There were some sporadic gunfire between the Serbs and Muslims. I don't know that there were any killings, that there were any casualties or victims. All the people sought refuge and shelter out of town, and we had to flee mostly because of that damn Drina and the water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. Madam, because you and counsel are both speaking the same language, there is a problem if you answer the question straight away. The interpreters are having difficulty keeping up with you, so if you would just pause just before you answer any question. Mr. Domazet, similarly pauses before he asks you a question to enable the interpreters who are giving it to us in English, your evidence in English and French. It enables them to catch up. So just pause before you answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What you have just described to us happened several days before the arrival of the army, or rather, the Uzice Corps to Visegrad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: After that, madam, you yourself returned to Visegrad, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Just a minute. I haven't finished my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you spent that entire time in Visegrad continuously; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During that time you worked in the factory in which you were employed before these events; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, then, and later, when you spoke about the car drive, you were driven by a driver from the company you worked for. It was the company driver and company car; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you something related to the event you described that took place in Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It is in connection with the fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. I'll be happy to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You saw a blow-up, an enlarged photograph, a moment ago of that part of town, of that part of Pionirska Street, in fact, which doesn't show the whole of Pionirska Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your house, your new house, the one you were talking about, is it on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is it above the photograph, if I can put it that way, that the photograph does not encompass it because your house was up above the area the photograph showed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: That part of town was the Pionirska Mahala, and my house is a new house in quite a different part of town which was not encompassed by the photograph at all. You cannot see it at all on that section shown on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I don't think you understood me, madam. You're now telling me about the house, your house, located on the other side of the Drina River; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: You mean my own personal house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you had a new house in Pionirska Street, a house that you yourself built together with your husband, which you were to have moved into, but you said that you actually never moved into it, that you actually never lived there, and you also said that you had another house in another part of town, not to mention the district, the area, but that that was on the other bank of the Drina, in quite a different section of town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, sir. No. Can I explain it myself, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Everything to do with Pionirska Street and that settlement, I was there renting. I rented the place there, whereas my own house, the house I owned and built together with my husband, was located in quite a different area, much higher up, on the other side, not across the Drina River but on the other side, on the opposite side. And I didn't spend one single night in my own house. It was a newly built house. All I have left is the keys in the door. I didn't succeed in moving in all my personal effects into the house ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well, madam. I understand. In Pionirska, you lived in a rented place and you had a landlord and you also lived in some other houses temporarily from time to time; is that right? Have I got it right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And the place you lived in as a tenant, can you see that house on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No. I'd need a larger photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it above or below Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: On the photograph -- the photograph doesn't even show the lower part of Pionirska Street, which, as far as I know, begins from a street leading from the centre of town towards the exit to town, in the direction of Uzice; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you explain, looking at Pionirska Street from the place it starts at, from the start of Pionirska Street upwards, where you saw, as you said, the column for the first time which Mitar Vasiljevic was with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: The place I put my cross on the photograph first. There's some streets missing there. There's the Smajlovic house there as well, to my left. Going up the street, on my left, would be the Smajlovic house. The man is in Sweden at the moment. His nickname is Tetak, and that's where he was from. And I said that a portion of this area on the photograph was missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think, madam, you placed a cross on the photograph of the place I asked you about, but now I understand that that isn't the spot, that the spot is actually lower down and can't be seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps four or five metres lower. I said straight away that a part of the picture was missing, or rather, the beginning of Pionirska Street wasn't on the photograph that was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, when you saw this group of people, as far as I was able to understand, you were moving in the same direction behind those people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What were Mitar Vasiljevic's movements? Was he moving behind the column? How long was the column or procession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Mitar was mostly towards the side. There was a large mass of people, and he had some assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That was to be my next question. Was he alone or were there other people with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: There were other people with him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us who those other people with him were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Well, of course there were lots of Mitar's assistants. All the Lukics were there, all the members of the Lukic; Vasiljevic, Lipovac, all their members. Many people. There was Sredoje Lukic, Niko Vujicic, and lots of people I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So this column of people from Koritnik were escorted, in addition to Mitar, by a larger group, and you said that amongst that group you recognised Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Niko Vujicic, but you also mentioned some Vasiljevics and Lipovacs. Can you tell us who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Vasiljevic. Perhaps his first name was Zoran. I don't remember exactly. Of the Lipovac there was Jovo, a very short man, of short build.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember what Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You can't remember at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How far were you behind that column, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Perhaps -- I was very near, actually. Ten metres, perhaps, until I turned by the garage. The column went off in front of me, upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that the entire time that you were behind the column, you were at a distance of ten metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but the whole thing didn't last very long, because the short street is a short one, not a very long street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, you were walking behind the column up until the place where you left it to go to the house you indicated on the photograph, whereas the column continued on its way with all these people up Pionirska Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned, madam, a person today who was coming towards you and who exchanged a few words with Mitar Vasiljevic. Can you tell me whether it was a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice a man doing the same thing, that is to say, talking to Mitar Vasiljevic, or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the woman? I think you said that you knew her.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, I remember her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us her name and surname? Or if you think that it is necessary, perhaps we can move into private session or perhaps we can just -- she could just give a name to identify the individual. I think it would be important for us to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Well, can I just give the first name? Can I just say the person's first name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Stop there anyway. You give us her first name. Are you worried about identifying her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I'll say the name. The lady's name was Hanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that lady alone or was she with anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: She was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would be helpful if we had the woman's full name, her first and last name, in view of the fact that the name, first name, Hanka, is what she was called. Perhaps her name was somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. Well, then, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. We're now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if it's time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It certainly is. I hadn't noticed the time. Thank you. We'll adjourn now and resume at 11.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: We are now in public session, so I would like to ask you about this person that we discussed a moment ago. Of course, don't mention her name, please. We all know the name now. I would like to ask you first whether you remember the spot where this occurred when you met her, starting from the beginning of Pionirska Street upwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: You mean going from the beginning of the street upwards? Maybe about -- someplace between the house I was living and the beginning, I think it was maybe halfway, midway between what was happening along this part of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So well into Pionirska Street. It was in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did this person see you? Did she greet you? Did you say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: We saw each other. We noticed one another. We didn't have any conversation at all. We said nothing to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So she saw you, you exchanged glances, and she went on towards town and you continued along your way down Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember what the weather was like that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean fine, clear, warm weather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes, fine weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When we're talking about the time of day, you said that from the moment you turned off towards the house where you spent that night in, that about half an hour later the explosions and the fire started, but you didn't tell us whether while you were moving along the street it was still daylight, or was it dusk or the beginning of darkness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was the beginning of the evening. Dark was just falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So while you were following the column and turning off the road, this was -- darkness was just falling.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Darkness was just falling. It was in the afternoon, early evening, about 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, when you were describing what happened the next day, in the morning, or rather, what you heard and saw, you said that a neighbour of yours, a Serb, was extending aid to a woman who had burns close to the creek.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is his name [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he live in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know his surname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I don't remember. I've forgotten it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember -- we're talking about the following day, in the morning. When was this? Was this early in the morning, later in the course of the morning, or some other time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: It was early in the morning. My working hours started at 7.00 a.m. I started work at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So this was before 7.00 as you were leaving for work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see or talk to the person who was injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were there any other people alive, injured or uninjured, in the vicinity of that house that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I didn't see anything. I didn't meet anyone in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see this woman or did you hear about it from this [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, let me repeat. You said that you didn't see anything in the morning when I asked you whether there were any other people, either injured or uninjured in the vicinity of the house, you said that you didn't see any. So my question is: Did you personally see this woman and your [redacted] or do you know about it from what he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: From what my [redacted] said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So he didn't tell you that he saw any other person except that woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He didn't say anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he recognised that person or that he knew her name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No. I didn't ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave to the investigator, you mentioned the name of that woman as being Ismeta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: According to later stories, apparently the surviving woman's name was Ismeta, and she is still alive.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator, you said, and I quote, "I also saw a woman in the grass who appeared to be alive. A local Serb whose name was [redacted], he was over 50, went up to help her. Later I heard that the woman's name was Ismeta." So is it true that you saw her or you only heard about it from this witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I heard all this from the witness [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, when you're talking about the incident that occurred on the bridge, when the victim was a certain Medo, you said that you were with the driver and that at the time you did not move around on foot but that your driver of the company car drove you around; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of that driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot tell you that, and I would really beg you: I cannot ever tell you that, because this means a lot for my life and my future.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he a Serb or a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you not want to give us his name because of any kind of danger he would be exposed to or is there another reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: There are many reasons, please, so that nothing should happen to that driver. That driver saved my life, my life and my daughter, and he took us from Visegrad, and so please, don't ask me anything else about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, perhaps I can have understanding for your concern, but please understand also that that person is a witness of something you told us about, and this can be very important for this case or maybe some other case. And for us it is invaluable for us to learn of all possible witnesses who, if necessary, would be equally protected as you are. So could you please give us the full name of that person in a private session, if necessary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: No, I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, as to relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's a collateral matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's hardly a collateral matter. You're relying on the incident that she said she saw and Mr. Domazet is seeking to obtain the name of the driver so they can interview him to see whether he will give the same evidence. How is that merely collateral?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is not one of the crimes that the accused was charged with

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Then why did you lead evidence of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Because it shows the time that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It clearly is relevant, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that we discuss, given the concerns that this witness has regarding this information, I'd ask that we go into private session and discuss this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. Let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You just said that you find it difficult to remember what happened seven days ago, but today you are testifying about events which occurred nine years ago without having testified about those events at all before this year. So is it possible that with regard to the events you spoke about today, your memory may be faulty, or do you insist that everything happened in the way you have described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG115
utterances.text: Everything I said in my statement is correct. As to whom I was with in the street, who was nearby, who was in front of me and who was behind me, it's only normal that I can't remember those things. It was a normal day and people were going about their business. My firm is rather a big one. Some people are doing -- taking one bridge, some another, some are going by car, some on foot. I mostly went by car for private problems that I had. When I didn't have a car, I had to go on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, when you were giving your statement to the investigator of the Prosecution, you mentioned, among other things, the names of people you knew, that you either personally saw or heard as having participated in certain activities in the area of Visegrad.
